Agents
Remote access — On. Agents in the cloud reach Olympus at relay.example.
Connect an agentLet ChatGPT, Claude, Grok or a coding agent ask Olympus, under the same privacy rules as your OpenClaw agent.

Connect an agent

Pick the agent you use. It never sees Private source text or Secrets. For Private items it receives only answers that Venice or a local model reasoned out, with each item's title, path, source and author.

Claude web, desktop and phone
  1. In Claude, open Customize, then Connectors. Choose +, then Add custom connector, name it Olympus, and paste this address as the URL:
    https://relay.example/mcp
  2. Choose Add, then Connect on the Olympus connector. An Olympus page opens in this computer's browser asking to connect Claude to Olympus: choose Connect. Do this in Claude on this computer; the page opens only here. After that, Olympus works in Claude on your phone too.
  3. Tell it when to ask Olympus. Paste this into a Claude project's instructions.
    Olympus is my private search over my own email, files, messages, notes, bookmarks and saved reading. Use it whenever my question might be answered from my own records: what someone told me, what a document or contract says, or when something happened. If you are not sure, use it anyway. You do not need me to mention Olympus. If Olympus lists an olympus_search tool, search with it: it returns matching excerpts from my records for you to answer from. If the first search misses, try once more with different words. Otherwise ask its source_answer tool, one question at a time, and pass on its answer. Answers can take a few minutes. If it says it is still working and gives you a job_id, call source_answer_result with that job_id, again while it says working. Do not ask the same question again. Answer only from what Olympus returns, with its citations, and say plainly what it could not find. Do not guess past it or fill gaps from memory. Use source_index_status only to check which of my sources are ready. Use ask_anonymously only when I ask you to send a question anonymously.
    The Olympus skill is the folder integrations/agent-skills/ask-olympus inside the plugin folder.
ChatGPT
  1. In ChatGPT, open Settings, then Apps, and turn on Developer mode under Advanced settings. Then create a connector, name it Olympus, choose OAuth, and paste this address as the URL:
    https://relay.example/mcp
  2. Choose Create. An Olympus page opens in this computer's browser asking to connect ChatGPT to Olympus: choose Connect. Do this in ChatGPT on this computer; the page opens only here.
  3. Tell it when to ask Olympus. Paste this into a ChatGPT project's instructions, or into your custom instructions.

Claude Code or Codex on this computer

These run on this computer, so they work without remote access. Paste this into Claude Code or Codex and it adds Olympus for you:

Add Olympus to this coding agent as a local MCP server. First find the full path of the olympus command: - If `openclaw plugins inspect olympus --json` finds the plugin, it is `<plugin.rootDir>/bin/olympus`. - Otherwise Olympus was installed with its Mac installer, and it is `$HOME/.local/bin/olympus` with $HOME written out. Check that the file exists. Then run the one command for this tool: - Claude Code: `claude mcp add olympus -- <olympus path> serve` - Codex: `codex mcp add olympus -- <olympus path> serve` Do not change any other configuration. Afterwards, list the Olympus tools to confirm source_answer is there.
Add it yourself instead

The olympus path is the full path of the olympus command. On a Mac set up with the Olympus installer it is ~/.local/bin/olympus, written out from your home folder. With OpenClaw it is bin/olympus inside the rootDir that openclaw plugins inspect olympus --json prints. For Claude Code, run:

claude mcp add olympus -- <olympus path> serve

For Codex, add this to ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.olympus] command = "<olympus path>" args = ["serve"]

To have it ask Olympus on its own, paste this into your CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, or copy the Olympus skill folder into ~/.claude/skills/ or ~/.codex/skills/.

[mcp_servers.olympus] command = "<olympus path>" args = ["serve"]

If the first search misses, try once more with different words. Otherwise ask its source_answer tool, one question at a time, and pass on its answer. Answers can take a few minutes. If it says it is still working and gives you a job_id, call source_answer_result with that job_id, again while it says working. Do not ask the same question again. Answer only from what Olympus returns, with its citations, and say plainly what it could not find. Do not guess past it or fill gaps from memory. Use source_index_status only to check which of my sources are ready. Use ask_anonymously only when I ask you to send a question anonymously.

Olympus never sends what it recognizes as a Secret to ChatGPT, and never answers from it. Olympus labels items automatically, and labels can be wrong.
